messages.subject: anyone know of a function to identify node numbers by phylogenetic definition?
messages.subject_clean: anyone know of a function to identify node numbers by phylogenetic definition?
messages.body_plain:
I'm trying to run Biogeobears over a bunch of trees that vary in topology and branch length (a set of likely trees from a bayesian analysis with many fossil tips). In order to summarize the results at particular nodes, I need to be able to identify the correct node numbers for particular clades, but I can't do that by using the mrca functions because the clade content is variable and the changes in topology change the node numbers.  I need to identify the most inclusive clade containing taxa X and Y, but not taxon Z. If anyone has experienced a similar problem or knows of r functions that might be able to help I'd love to hear them!

Joey

messages.body_plain:
Hi Joey!

I have some code for this but it's not in the package yet.  But if you have some R skillz it's not too hard.  A handy function that is in BioGeoBEARS is
prt():

tr = read.tree(file="whatever.newick")
prt(tr)

...this converts a tree to a much handier table format.

If you do:

===============================
tr_table = prt(tr, printflag=FALSE, get_tipnames=TRUE)
tr_table
===============================

...then this column:

tr_table$tipnames

...will have, for each node in the tree, a string with the alphabetical, comma-delimited list of species descending from that node.

Since each list is alphabetical, you can just match strings to match nodes between two trees...

Cheers!
Nick

messages.subject_clean: [BioGeoBEARS] anyone know of a function to identify node numbers by phylogenetic definition?
messages.body_plain:
Awesome! prt is very helpful. Here is what I came up with, operating on the knowledge that the lowest numbered node that contains two taxa of interest should always have the most total taxa.

mostinclusive() returns the node number of the most inclusive clade containing taxon1 and taxon2, but not taxon3. taxon names should be in quotes when calling the function, e.g. mostinclusive(tree,"taxon1","taxon2","taxon3")

mostinclusive <- function(tree,taxon1, taxon2, taxon3){
tr_table = prt(tree, printflag=FALSE, get_tipnames=TRUE)
taxon1matches=grep(taxon1,tr_table$tipnames)
taxon2matches=grep(taxon2,tr_table$tipnames)
taxon3matches=grep(taxon3,tr_table$tipnames)
commonclades=intersect(taxon1matches,taxon2matches)
removetaxon3=setdiff(commonclades,taxon3matches)
inclusive=min(removetaxon3)
return(inclusive)
}

Thanks again,
Joey

messages.subject: 4 published papers using BioGeoBEARS
messages.body_plain:
Hi group,

At the June 2014 SMBE meeting, I ran into Rebecca Harris, who mentioned that her paper using BioGeoBEARS had been published. This encouraged me to look for other such publications. There are already at least four!

http://phylo.wikidot.com/publications-using-biogeobears
====================================
Publications using BioGeoBEARS

1. Rebecca B. Harris, SM Birks, AD Leaché (2014). "Incubator birds: biogeographical origins and evolution of underground nesting in megapodes (Galliformes: Megapodiidae)." Journal of Biogeography, http://dx.doi.org/10.1111/jbi.12357 http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jbi.12357/full

2. G Voelker, JV Peñalba, JW Huntley, RCK Bowie (2014). "Diversification in an Afro-Asian songbird clade (Erythropygia–Copsychus) reveals founder-event speciation via trans-oceanic dispersals and a southern to northern colonization pattern in Africa." Molecular Phylogenetics and Evolution, 73, 97–105. http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.ympev.2014.01.024 http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1055790314000372

3. Janet C. Buckner, Jessica Lynch Alfaro, Anthony B. Rylands, Michael E. Alfaro (2014). "Biogeography of the marmosets and tamarins (Callitrichidae). Molecular Phylogenetics and Evolution, Available online 20 May 2014. http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.ympev.2014.04.031 http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1055790314001596

4. R. Eduardo Palma, Dusan Boric-Bargetto, J. Pablo Jayat, David A. Flores, Horacio Zeballos, Víctor Pacheco, Ricardo A. Cancino, Fernando D. Alfaro, Enrique Rodríguez-Serrano, Ulyses F. J. Pardiñas (2014). "Molecular phylogenetics of mouse opossums: new findings on the phylogeny of Thylamys (Didelphimorphia, Didelphidae)." Zoological Scripta, 43(3), 217-234. May 2014. http://dx.doi.org/10.1111/zsc.12051 http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/zsc.12051/full

Other citations of BioGeoBEARS

1. Catanach, Therese (2014). Biogeography and phylogenetics of grassland Auchenorrhyncha. Ph.D. thesis, School of Integrative Biology, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign. January 16, 2014. http://hdl.handle.net/2142/46689 https://www.ideals.illinois.edu/handle/2142/46689
====================================

If you happen to get something accepted, let me know and I will add it to the list.  Cheers! Nick
